processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum-induction-melted 28Mn0Ni ingot was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h before hot rolling.
After homogenization the ingot was hot rolled at 1323 K; final hot rolled plate thickness ~13 mm. This condition is denoted HR.

Samples cut from hot-rolled plates were cold rolled at room temperature in several passes to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets); the state is denoted HR+CR. Cold reduction was capped at 50% for all three alloys (15Mn5Ni cracked beyond 50%) to allow comparison at a common degree of cold work.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenite (γ, FCC) Ni-free low-density steel in the hot rolled + 50% cold rolled (HR+CR) condition. Austenite grains are equiaxed (in HR) and mostly deformed by planar slip, as reflected by parallel slip bands; no traces of deformation twinning or martensite transformation. No second phase (B2) is present.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains in HR condition; grains deformed by planar slip after cold rolling
phases_present.grain_size: 5–7 μm (equiaxed γ-matrix grain size in HR condition)
phases_present.texture: nearly random texture in HR condition

defects.type: planar slip bands (parallel slip bands from planar slip deformation)

defect_interactions.interaction_type: planar slip (dislocation glide on parallel slip planes)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Cold rolling produced parallel planar slip bands within the austenite grains, indicating that austenite deformed mostly by planar slip; no deformation twinning or martensite was observed.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Austenite deformed mostly by planar slip as reflected by parallel slip bands; no deformation twinning and no martensite transformation.
interfaces.interface_notes: 28Mn0Ni is single-phase austenite in the HR+CR condition, so there are no phase interfaces; the strain is accommodated by intragranular planar slip.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Bulk Vickers hardness, AFFRI Vickers tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s; hardness averaged over ten measurements per sample.

measurement_conditions.strain_rate: ~3 × 10^-4 s^-1 (initial); constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm min^-1
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat tensile specimens, gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests triplicated for each condition; average of three readings reported.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve of 28Mn0Ni in HR+CR (50% cold reduction) shown in Fig. 9a; strength rises steeply to ~1450–1500 MPa within ~0.02 strain with negligible strain hardening.
strain_hardening_rate: negligible strain hardening; uniform strain (just before necking) less than 3%

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: After 50% cold reduction all three alloys attained similar strength levels/hardness, but the maximum rate of work hardening occurred in the single-phase (Ni-free) 28Mn0Ni alloy; at 50% cold reduction the hardness of 15Mn5Ni was ~20 VHN higher than that of 28Mn0Ni.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) equipped with Oxford EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors; samples polished to colloidal silica ~100 nm surface finish; TSL-OIM software
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Step size 120 nm (fine-grained) or 250 nm (coarse-grained) over ~100×100 μm² and ~200×200 μm² areas; three scans per sample; KAM and GOS of 2° criterion used to delineate recrystallized microstructure; Σ3 CSL boundaries for twin fraction.
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze microstructure, phase distribution, grain orientations, grain size and twin fractions of cold rolled samples.
characterization_methods.key_findings: For 28Mn0Ni in HR+CR: single-phase austenite (phase map uniformly FCC); equiaxed randomly oriented grains with parallel planar slip bands visible in the image quality map; no deformation twinning or martensite.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument, Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Selected samples in HR+CR condition; 2θ range 40–120°
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of cold rolled and heat-treated samples.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni alloy in the cold rolled (HR+CR) condition showed peaks corresponding to γ-phase only (single-phase austenite).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Dwell time 15 s; ASTM E-140-02; hardness averaged over ten measurements per sample; room temperature
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate the change in bulk hardness with degree of cold rolling.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni hardness increased with cold reduction and saturated to ~450 VHN at 50% cold reduction.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm min^-1 (initial strain rate ~3 × 10^-4 s^-1); flat specimens gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm; ASTM E8M; tests triplicated.
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate strength and ductility of the chosen alloys in different processing conditions.
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni in HR+CR (50% cold reduction): YS 1350 ± 10 MPa, UTS 1500 ± 10 MPa, TE 10 ± 0.4 %, with negligible strain hardening (uniform strain <3%).

unmapped_findings: The equal-channel-free cold rolling route was applied to all three alloys for a common degree of cold work; all three alloys could be rolled successfully without cracking at room temperature up to 50% reduction in thickness, whereas the 15Mn5Ni alloy cracked beyond 50% reduction (reason for capping reduction at 50%).

In the parent hot rolled (HR) condition the 28Mn0Ni alloy hardness was reported as ~256 ± 5 VHN; the hardness rose with cold reduction and saturated to ~450 VHN at 50% reduction (this HR value is the 0% cold-reduction start point for the current HR+CR sample's process chain).

The 28Mn0Ni alloy is described as the Ni-free reference composition that is single-phase austenite in the hot rolled condition and B2-free (B2 volume fraction 0), in contrast to the Ni-containing grades that contain B2 stringers.
Nominal/measured composition of the 28Mn0Ni alloy (Table 1, wt.%): Mn 28.3 ± 0.4, Al 9.0 ± 0.05, C 0.9 ± 0.01, Ni not detected (Ni-free), Fe balance.
